models.name: Model A: High-fidelity partitioned FSI with anisotropic leaflet shells
models.what_it_computes: Cycle-averaged coaptation area, maximum principal leaflet stress, and diastolic transvalvular pressure–flow response

models.name: Model B: Immersed-boundary FSI with reduced-order hemodynamics
models.what_it_computes: Instantaneous coaptation gap metric, leaflet membrane stress proxy, and effective orifice dynamics

models.name: Model C: Monolithic ALE FSI with nonlinear fiber-reinforced leaflets
models.what_it_computes: Leaflet contact pressure distribution during closure, peak von Mises stress, and strain energy over the cardiac cycle

mechanisms.name: Annular dilation
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Root enlargement reduces leaflet overlap, risking regurgitation and elevated edge stresses during diastolic loading.

mechanisms.name: Leaflet stiffening
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Material thickening and increased modulus alter deformation, shifting stress concentrations and impairing coaptation.

mechanisms.name: Commissural misalignment
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Rotational offset of commissures disrupts symmetric closure, creating gaps and localized stress risers.

deviation.detail: All factor scores are reported on a 0–5 numeric credibility scale with predefined acceptance thresholds.

expected_decision.outcome_source: Because one or more topics for several model–mechanism combinations do not meet the acceptance thresholds, and because the most challenging mechanism—commissural misalignment—remains insufficiently supported by data and physics fidelity relative to the intended decisions, the credibility assessment outcome is Not accepted.
rationale_keywords: do not meet the acceptance thresholds

models: Model A: High-fidelity partitioned FSI with anisotropic leaflet shells
Model B: Immersed-boundary FSI with reduced-order hemodynamics
Model C: Monolithic ALE FSI with nonlinear fiber-reinforced leaflets
requirements: We employed a private 0–5 numeric credibility scale to grade evidence for each topic, separately for each model × mechanism pairing.

The thresholds selected a priori were: for numerical sufficiency, a score of 4 was required (refinements change key outputs less than approximately 1% for areas and less than 3% for peak stresses); for solver stability, 4 (tight residuals with energy or mass imbalance less than approximately 0.7% per cycle); for physics adequacy, 4 (quantitative agreement across at least two outputs within 10% error, with deviations explained); for parameter adequacy, 3.5 (well-justified distributions with local or global sensitivity documented and posterior predictive checks at least for one mechanism); for test environment representativeness, 3.5 (waveform RMS errors less than 5 mmHg and Womersley similarity within 5% with mechanism-specific fidelity); and for device sample breadth, 3 (at least four devices per mechanism or equivalent justification of statistical power).

expected_context_of_use: The context of use is preclinical design evaluation at the component level to support engineering decisions about design margins against regurgitation and fatigue-critical stress risers, not direct patient-specific therapy decisions.
